4. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the findings that although plaintiff has successfully proved his right, title and interest in the land in suit but he has failed to prove his possession in the land in suit and as such the suit so framed is not maintainable since he was required to seek declaration of title to the property in suit and also for khas possession, that the suit is also barred by limitation and the suit is bad for non-joinder of party since Administrator of Waqfs was required to be implead as party in the suit. 

 5. On appeal the appellate Court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the findings that the plaintiffs have right, title and interest in the land in suit and that as the defendants raised claim in the land in suit on the basis of kabalas obtained from the person having no title and as on the basis thereof dispossessed the plaintiff as such plaintiff is entitled to have the suit decreed on payment of advalorem court fee and also entitled to seek recovery of khas possession and that the plaintiff is also entitled to have the declaration that the kabalas are void, fraudulent, illegal and inoperative. Thereupon the defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction.
